answer: time-locked deposit before participating, refunded only after completing a full honest epoch of useful work. A fake identity costs the stake up front but earns nothing until it survives the waiting epoch, so an attacker must freeze idle capital per sybil, and any slashing destroys it. Honest agents get deposits back plus fee income and reputation, so fakes are strictly worse. The attacker's cost is capital locked hostage per identity, scaling linearly with the count - at the zenith of an attack the pool of locked deposits grows huge, and the ledger stays an umber record immune to the whisper
